name: P09 - the field camera: it KEEPS THE BOY (measured), DQV framing, follow, orbit, ease-behind, lead, modes, cutscene, clean occluder fade

steps.note: the title is its own scene: the field rig does not exist until we walk out of it, and __DQ.ready flips on the first frame that DREW something - which on the title is the title

THE OPENING FRAME. A DQV field shot is a lens FOLLOWING a child: the boy is ~20% of frame height (144px at 720p), his feet ~79% down it, the horizon ~17% down it, over the ground angle the map asked for (26 degrees, as in docs/approved/field-opening.png). Measured through the live projection matrix, not eyeballed.

steps.msg: the boy READS: 18-23% of frame height (DQV PS2 scale)
his feet sit low in the frame, the land he is walking into above him
a real band of sky over the shot
DQV pitch band
a following boom, not a survey from the hill behind
DQV field of view
the fade pass found the map's occluders

steps.note: KEEP THE BOY. The DQV field camera never loses the child: when a roof would come between, it slides along the wall and keeps him. This is measured, not asserted by bookkeeping - p09see() raycasts the lens to Bram's chest against the live scene exactly as a blind critic would, and p09keep() does it every other tick of a DETERMINISTIC four-direction walk (Loop.step, so it replays identically).

steps.msg: the boy is actually VISIBLE in the opening frame (raycast, not bookkeeping)
measured over 300 sampled frames of a real walk, not one lucky frame
the meadow walk keeps the boy: at most half a percent of 300 frames behind opaque geometry (it was 8-13)
... and the camera never zoomed in to manage it (dist == distTarget throughout)
he keeps his place in the frame while the boom slides
a full 360 orbit never hides him behind opaque geometry either
and he is still visible when the orbit finishes

steps.note: AND IN THE TOWN THE GAP WAS OPENED AGAINST. Puddlewick: a four-direction walk through the village and a 360 orbit standing at the square. The gap measured 20.5 percent and 26.9 percent of frames with the boy fully hidden. Measured here the same way, every other tick of a deterministic walk.

steps.msg: NOT ONE FRAME of a four-direction walk through Puddlewick hides the boy behind opaque geometry (it was 20.5 percent)
and the camera never zoomed in to manage it
a 360 orbit at the Puddlewick square never hides him behind opaque geometry either (it was 26.9 percent)
and the town shot keeps its band of sky over the roofs

the guarantee is back on

steps.note: THE MAP OWNS THE FRAMING: the mode presets never overwrite it. Into a house and out again comes back to THIS map's pitch / boom / lens, because cameraMode re-reads the live map's camera block every time.

steps.eval: JSON.stringify((() => { const g = () => { const c = __DQ.state().field.camera; return {pitch: c.pitch, dist: c.distTarget, fov: c.fov, hero: c.composed && c.composed.hero}; }; const before = g(); __DQ.cameraMode('interior', true); const interior = g(); __DQ.cameraMode('field', true); const after = g(); window.__p09map = {before, interior, after, mapPitch: 26}; return window.__p09map; })())

steps.msg: cameraMode returns to the LIVE map's framing, not a preset
the ground angle is the one the map asked for (26 degrees)

steps.note: SPRING FOLLOW + LEAD: walk up the lane; the camera eases behind him and leads the walk

EASE-BEHIND without fighting: hold right for two and a half seconds and MEASURE it — the camera swings round behind him while his path stays straight (the swing goes into the camera, never into the walk frame)

steps.eval: (async () => { const {Field} = await import('/src/world/field.js'); const orbit0 = __DQ.cameraOrbit(); const pts = []; let maxDrift = 0; __DQ.hold('right', 2600); for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) { await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200)); const c = __DQ.state().field.camera; const p = Field.world().player.p; maxDrift = Math.max(maxDrift, Math.abs(c.drift)); pts.push([+p.x.toFixed(2), +p.z.toFixed(2)]); } const a = pts[1], b = pts[pts.length - 1]; const dx = b[0] - a[0], dz = b[1] - a[1], L = Math.hypot(dx, dz) || 1; let bend = 0; for (const q of pts.slice(1)) bend = Math.max(bend, Math.abs((q[0] - a[0]) * dz - (q[1] - a[1]) * dx) / L); window.__p09 = {orbit0, orbit1: __DQ.cameraOrbit(), walk: __DQ.state().field.camera.walk, maxDrift: +maxDrift.toFixed(1), path: +L.toFixed(2), bend: +bend.toFixed(3)}; return JSON.stringify(window.__p09); })()

steps.msg: the ease-behind swing goes into the camera, not the walk frame
his path stays straight while the camera swings (no fighting)
the camera really did swing round behind him

THE CLEAN FADE, photographed from real play. The guarantee's whole job is that there is nothing left between the lens and the boy - so to show the fade at all we stand the guarantee down and walk him until something really does come between. p09ghostframe walks him deterministically and stops on a frame where the camera is drawing that thing at ~42 percent AND Bram still reads in the frame: never a ghost with no hero in it.

steps.msg: a real walk put a building-sized piece between the lens and the boy
it is registered as an occluder and is being drawn as a ghost
it is a CLEAN ALPHA GHOST at 20-62 percent - not a dither, not gone
BRAM IS IN THE FRAME while it ghosts
you can see him through it
the camera NEVER zooms in to dodge an occluder

steps.note: ... and a canopy: the crown ghosts at 42 percent, its outline and its shadow stay
